name: Question 5
problem:
Consider the d’Alembert differential equation

$$
y=xcos\,(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})-3\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Using the substitution $t=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ the equation can be transformed to a first-order linear equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+P(t)x=Q(t).
$$

Find the functions $P$ and $Q.$

$\,\,P(t)=$
{{field-1}}$,\,Q(t)=$
{{field-2}}
worked_solution:
A differential equation is a d'Alembert differential equation if it can be expressed in the form

$$
y=xf({y}^{′})+g({y}^{′}),
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are differentiable functions of ${y}^{′}.$ 

In our case, we wish to transform the equation

$$
y=xcos\,(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})-3\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}
$$

into a first-order linear equation for $x=x(t).$ We proceed in three steps:

**Step 1**: Substitute, and differentiate with respect to $x.$

We have the substitution

$$
t=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Substituting this into the equation gives

$$
y=x\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-3t.
$$

Differentiating both sides with respect to $x,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-3t).\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum and product rules and using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3t) \\ t & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x)+x\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))-\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3t) \\ t & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\frac{\text{d}t}{\text{d}x}-3\frac{\text{d}t}{\text{d}x}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Isolate the derivative and take its reciprocal.

We isolate $\frac{\text{d}t}{\text{d}x}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t) & =-x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\frac{\text{d}t}{\text{d}x}-3\frac{\text{d}t}{\text{d}x} \\ t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t) & =-(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+3)\frac{\text{d}t}{\text{d}x} \\ -\frac{t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)}{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+3} & =\frac{\text{d}t}{\text{d}x}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}t}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t}{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+3}.
$$

Therefore, by taking the reciprocal of each side, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+3}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t}.
$$

**Step 3**: Express the derivative as a first-order linear equation.

Finally, we write this in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+P(t)x=Q(t)
$$

as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+3}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t} \\ (\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+3 \\ (\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t)\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & =3 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}-\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t} & =\frac{3}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t} \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)}{t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)} & =\frac{3}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(t)=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)}{t-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)},\,Q(t)=\frac{3}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-t}.
$$

Question 5
?
Consider the d’Alembert differential equation y=xcos(dydx)−3dydx.

Using the substitution t=dydx, the equation can be transformed to a first-order linear equation of the form dxdt+P(t)x=Q(t).

Find the functions P and Q.

P(t)=
sin⁡(t)t−cos⁡(t)
sin⁡(t)t−cos⁡(t)
−sin⁡(t)t−cos⁡(t)
cos⁡(t)t−sin⁡(t)
sin⁡(t)cos⁡(t)−t
,Q(t)=
3cos⁡(t)−t
1cos⁡(t)−t
3t−cos⁡(t)
−3t+cos⁡(t)
3cos⁡(t)−t
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A differential equation is a d'Alembert differential equation if it can be expressed in the form y=xf(y′)+g(y′), where f and g are differentiable functions of y′.

In our case, we wish to transform the equation y=xcos(dydx)−3dydx into a first-order linear equation for x=x(t). We proceed in three steps:

Step 1: Substitute, and differentiate with respect to x.

We have the substitution t=dydx.

Substituting this into the equation gives y=xcos⁡(t)−3t.
